Illinois Solar Decathlon (ISD) has assembled a team of 28 engineers and architects to assess and design a complete energy retrofit of an existing home at Allerton Park, a University of Illinois property. The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Race to Zero Student Design Competition (Race to Zero) is engaging undergraduate students, graduate students, and university faculty to become part of a new leadership movement to achieve truly sustainable homes.

As part of DOE’s Building America and Zero Energy Ready Home programs, the Race to Zero (formerly known as the Challenge Home Student Design Competition) was designed to:

- Inspire and develop the next generation of building science professionals.
- Advance and enhance building science curriculum in universities.
- Complement the experiential learning benefits provided by the U.S. Department of Energy Solar 
- Decathlon through an additional collegiate competition opportunity. 

The Sun Catcher Cottage project will be presented to the Race to Zero judging panel in Denver, Colorado on April 18, 2015.

I am a seasoned research and insights team leader and professional with 15 + years of experience in unpacking user /customer insights to answer business strategy, branding, customer and product design questions. publications.title: Tailoring lignin nanoparticle properties: the effects of pH and salt on shape and antioxidant capacity
publications.publishedAt: Royal Society of Chemistry Sustainability · Feb 6, 2024
publications.description: In this study we explore the extent to which we can tune lignin nanoparticles produced in a biorefinery that couples a microbial electrolysis cell to lignin depolymerization. We vary the salt type and pH and monitor the size and shape of the nanoparticles, as well as the antioxidant capacity of the mixture. We found that the salt type influences the shape of the lignin nanoparticles – ranging from spherical (phosphate) to rod-like (nitrate and chloride) and flower-like (carbonate). Additionally, the shape and the size influence the antioxidant capacity due to changes in the surface area to volume ratio. The flower-like nanoparticles have a high surface area to volume ratio and the highest antioxidant capacity, which is similar to that of the industrial benchmark antioxidant, Trolox. The antioxidant capacity of the lignin nanoparticles illustrates their high potential value in the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, personal care, and agricultural industries.

publications.title: The effects of lignin source and extraction on the composition and properties of biorefined depolymerization products
publications.publishedAt: Royal Society of Chemistry Sustainability · Oct 26, 2023
publications.description: We explore the efficacy of depolymerization as a function of lignin source and extraction method under the conditions of our previously described biorefinery. Biomass source (i.e. herbaceous, softwood, and hardwood) influences the total available lignin and structural features such as the ratio of monomers (S/G) and the percentage of β-O-4 linkage. The method of extraction (i.e. Milled Wood (mild), Organosolv (medium), and Klason (harsh)) determines levels of solubilization, preservation of the intrinsic lignin structure, and distribution and properties of products. Herbaceous lignin extracted by the Organosolv process is best suited for depolymerization in our biorefinery and shows the greatest extent of solubilization (∼100% over 7 days), the highest yields of phenolics and flavonoids, and the most and smallest lignin nanoparticles. Additionally, this depolymerized product mixture has the highest antioxidant capacity. Only the harsh, Klason method successfully isolates lignin, through carbohydrate conversion, from all three sources, but the herbaceous and hardwood sources are depolymerized to a lesser extent than by the Organosolv method. With low density of labile bonds, softwood lignin is not effectively depolymerized under these conditions. Although modifying intrinsic lignin structure the least, Milled Wood lignin does not efficiently extract lignin from any of the biomass, and the extracted lignin is low in purity inhibiting further processing. These results further detail the promise of herbaceous Organosolv lignin as a renewable feedstock to high value products in a distributed-scale biorefinery.

publications.title: Chapter 17 - Biorefining renewable aromatic carbon: Unlocking lignin's potential to produce high-value products
publications.publishedAt: Photosynthesis From Plants to Nanomaterials A volume in Nanomaterial-Plant Interactions · Aug 8, 2023
publications.description: Lignin is the largest store of renewable aromatic carbon on earth. Due to its recalcitrant nature, it is often burned as a low-value fuel rather than utilized for its full chemical potential. In this book chapter, we discuss a range of topics from the structure of lignin to potential applications of lignin-derived products. The structure of lignin depends on the source, and is further modified by the method with which it is extracted from the source. Both source and extraction methods have major influences on the ease, extent, and products of subsequent depolymerization. The various extraction methods, with special attention to their impact on the efficacy of lignin biorefining and base catalyzed depolymerization, are considered in depth. Finally, the production of high value products, such as flavonoids and lignin nanoparticles, is fully discussed, as well as potential applications across various industries, particularly their use as antioxidants in pharmaceuticals.

publications.title: Valorization of Lignin under Mild Conditions: Biorefining Flavonoids and Lignin Nanoparticles
publications.publishedAt: ACS Sustainable Chemistry and Engineering · Dec 29, 2022
publications.description: Lignin is the largest store of renewable aromatics. Due to its refractory nature, however, its chemical potential is not fully realized. Here, we propose a biorefinery where the treatment of wastewater by a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) produces “clean” water and a caustic catholyte that can depolymerize lignin under mild conditions into two high-value product streams. We determine the MEC operating conditions to produce a depolymerization solvent and quantify solution and colloidal phase products using an array of analytical techniques. In contrast to previous reports of limited high-value product yields, we obtain discrete aromatics (monomers and flavonoids) at 17% of initial lignin mass with bulk chemical analyses (11% for identified compounds using LC–MSn). In part, our higher product yield is due to selective repolymerization to form flavonoids. We simultaneously produce lignin nanoparticles and close mass balance. Both flavonoids and lignin nanoparticles have potential applications in the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, personal care, and agricultural industries.

publications.title: Formin Cdc12's specific actin assembly properties are tailored for cytokinesis in fission yeas
publications.description:
Kaitlin E Homa, Vilmos Zsolnay, Caitlin A Anderson, Meghan E O’Connell, Erin M Neidt, Gregory A Voth, Tamara C Bidone, David R Kovar
Cytokinesis, the physical separation of a mother cell into daughter cells, is a critical last step of
the cell division cycle. Defects can negatively impact development or lead to the proliferation of
cancer. The actin assembly factor formin facilitates cytokinetic contractile ring formation in
eukaryotic cells by determining both how often and how fast actin filaments assemble. We
investigated the importance of formin’s specific actin assembly properties on cytokinesis in
fission yeast, a model for cell division. By altering formin properties using a computational model and by engineering mutant fission yeast strains, we conclude that efficient actin filament
nucleation is the most critical factor for proper contractile ring formation.

publications.title: Structural basis for polarized elongation of actin filaments
publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences · Nov 18, 2020
publications.description:
V Zsolnay, HH Katkar, SZ Chou, TD Pollard, GA Voth
Eukaryotic cells utilize actin filaments to move, change shape, divide, and transport cargo. Decades of experiments have established that actin filaments elongate and shorten significantly faster from one end than the other, but the underlying mechanism for this asymmetry has not been explained. We used molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the structures of the actin filament ends in the ATP, ADP plus γ-phosphate, and ADP nucleotide states. We characterize the structures of actin subunits at both ends of the filament, explain the mechanisms leading to these differences, and connect the divergent structural properties of the two ends to their distinct polymerization rate constants.

publications.title: Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Ca2+ Release Uses a Cascading Network of Intra-SR and Channel Countercurrents
publications.description:
Zsolnay V, Fill M, Gillespie D
In muscle, Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) into the cytosol is mediated through the ryanodine receptors (RyRs) and sustained by countercurrents that keep the SR membrane potential near 0 mV. Likewise, Ca2+ reuptake by the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase pump requires countercurrent. Although evidence has suggested that TRIC K+ channels and/or RyR K+ influx provide these countercurrents, the exact sources have not yet been determined. We used an equivalent circuit compartment model of a cardiac SR, the surrounding cytosol, and the dyadic cleft to probe the sources of countercurrent during a complete cardiac cycle. By removing and relocating TRIC K+ channels, as well as limiting when they are active, we explored the various possible sources of SR countercurrent under many conditions. Our simulations indicate that no single channel type is essential for countercurrent. Rather, a cascading network of countercurrents is present with anion fluxes within the SR redistributing charges throughout the full SR volume. This allows ion channels in the entire SR membrane, far from the Ca2+ fluxes through the RyRs in the junctional SR and sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase pump in the nonjunctional SR, to mediate countercurrents that support Ca2+ release and reuptake. This multifactorial network of countercurrents allows Ca2+ release to be remarkably robust.

publications.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Bioresorbable Zinc/WC Nanocomposite Springs for Short Bowel Syndrome Treatment
publications.description: Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) is a devastating disease that affects thousands of lives every year. Patients diagnosed with SBS have malabsorption. Recently, endoscopically inserted springs were used to lengthen the small intestines. However, the springs are not biodegradable and need to be surgically removed after lengthening. Zinc, as a novel biodegradable material with suitable corrosion rate, is promising for this application. unfortunately, zinc lacks the mechanical strength to be used as effective springs. In this study, we successfully designed and fabricated a biodegradable Zn-WC nanocomposite spring with enhanced and tunable mechanical strengths to meet with requirements of springs for in vivo animal testing.

publications.title: Mileage efficiency of cars
publications.description:
Mileage efficiency of cars Patankar, N.A., Lin, J., Patankar, T.N., Mileage efficiency of cars, Cleaner Engineering and Technology (2021),
doi: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clet.2021.100240

This paper proposes a mileage efficiency metric to enable direct comparison of energy efficiency and greenhouse gas emission of cars for various vehicle mass, fuel type, vehicle make, vehicle technology, road infrastructure, and drive schedule. This metric allows a unifying measure of vehicle mileage and fuel consumption regardless of the above factors. The proposed mileage efficiency metric is based on the concept of an ideal car (IC), which is defined as the one without internal or external losses; or an ideal powertrain car, which is defined as the one without internal losses. Mileage efficiency is defined as the ratio of a real-world car (RWC) fuel economy (in miles per gasoline gallon equivalent or mpgge) to that of an ideal car. As such, mileage efficiency is able to attribute efficiency loss of a RWC to internal and/or external losses. It is shown that mileage efficiency depends on car design and shows how good or bad RWCs are relative to ICs. The paper also highlights the importance of good road infrastructures in reducing transportation fuel consumption independent of fuel efficiencies of cars. This work provides a fundamental framework to set government policies and incentives for vehicle technology, alternative fuel choice, and infrastructure investments.

about:
David is a multi-disciplined business professional with experience in consulting, corporate finance, strategy, business operations, and marketing. His career spans the retail, agency, and management consulting sectors. He is driven by a passion for delivering results at innovative companies.

David is currently working at Bain & Company, a global management consulting firm that advises executives across various industries. After several years of client-facing work, he jumped at the opportunity to help Bain innovate across its core products. He helped establish Bain's first centralized innovation capability and served as the portfolio manager. After two years, David was tapped to lead Strategy & Business Operations for Bain's internal software development group, Next Gen Software Solutions.

Previously, David was a senior digital analyst at Catalyst, a direct and digital marketing agency, a website analyst at Lands’ End, and the Founder of Roll On 2 Media, a DVD re-distributor that sold through eBay. He has also completed freelance analytics work for a top 10 MBA program and several eCommerce start-ups.

David holds an MBA from Johnson at Cornell University, where he graduated with honors (top 10%), and a BBA in business operations from the University of Wisconsin - Whitewater. He was an enthusiastic contributor while at Johnson, holding positions in the Consulting Club and Student Council, as well as volunteering as a Career Workgroup Leader, Admissions Ambassador, and Student Blogger.

David was recognized as one of the top “30 under 30” by DM News in 2011 and has published articles on Adage.com and CMO.com.

David has completed the Madison City Marathon and has a collection of over 75 board games. He is a native Wisconsinite and currently resides in Chicago.

The United States Coast Guard Academy (USCGA), located in New London, Connecticut, is the U.S. service academy specifically for the United States Coast Guard. Founded in 1876, the academy provides education to future Coast Guard officers in one of nine major fields of study.

Students are officers-in-training, and are referred to as cadets. Upon graduation, cadets receive a Bachelor of Science degree and commission in the U.S. Coast Guard as an ensign. In exchange for their debt-free education valued at over $500,000, graduates incur a five-year active-duty service obligation,[Notes 1] with additional years if the graduate attends flight school or subsequent government-funded graduate school. Out of approximately 300 cadets entering the academy each summer, around 250 graduate. Cadets choose from nine majors, with a curriculum that is graded according to their performance in a holistic program of academics, military bearing, physical fitness, character, and leadership. - Wikipedia

experience.companyName: Center for Arctic Study and Policy at the U.S. Coast Guard Academy
experience.description:
The Center for Arctic Study & Policy (CASP) develops and executes research and analysis to support U.S. Coast Guard missions and national policy and strategic objectives in the Arctic.  The Center helps stakeholders work together – including specialists from academia, government, indigenous peoples and organizations, non-governmental organizations, industry, international allies and partners, and the U.S. Coast Guard.

CASP supports Coast Guard interests in the Arctic through research, partnerships, and education. These efforts are focused on Coast Guard presence in the Arctic – to ensure safe, secure, and environmentally responsible maritime activity in this complex, changing environment.

At the Academy, CASP leads interdisciplinary efforts in the academic division, with Coast Guard sponsors and external partners, to develop solutions to maritime challenges in this region.  CASP is situated in the Academy’s Office of Scholarship, Research, and Innovation. - CASP website

The Summer Diplomatic Academy is an exceptional opportunity for those interested in international engagement to learn from career ambassadors with decades of experience. The world needs diplomacy more than ever, and WIDA aims to train the next generation of diplomats.
This unique and intensive practical professional training program introduces undergraduate and graduate students, as well as recent graduates, to careers in international diplomacy and teaches key skill sets. It covers the fundamentals of diplomatic practice and focuses on real-world aspects of work in embassies, consulates, government agencies, international organizations and global NGOs. The material emphasizes a skills-based and experiential-learning approach, and is generally not offered at colleges and universities.

Our instructors are ambassadors and other professional diplomats who have served in dozens of countries around the world. They teach the skills they learned by practicing diplomacy and managing international relations for decades, with simulation exercises and case studies derived from their own careers. They provide invaluable first-hand insight into policy-making and implementation, diplomatic protocol, the functions and management of embassies and consulates, diplomatic reporting and writing, negotiation and mediation, political and economic tradecraft, public diplomacy, cross-cultural communication and other competencies.

Short of actually working in diplomacy, there is no other place to learn what we teach. The program also includes career-counseling sessions. Students receive certificates from the Academy. - WIDA website

The Downtown Sailing Center (DSC) is an award-winning, nonprofit 501 (c)(3) community sailing center on a mission to make the sport of sailing accessible to EVERYONE! 

We have been offering sailing instruction and access to sailing to the greater Baltimore community since 1994.

The Downtown Sailing Center programs are available to the entire community. For adults, we offer adult education including accessible sailing; recreational sailing open sails; Thursday Night Racing and cruising. For youth, we offer summer camp, community outreach programming and our Young Mariners work force development program.

The DSC is a certified Community Sailing Center and accredited Sailing School through US Sailing, the national governing body of sailing. The DSC was recognized by US Sailing as the Outstanding New Program in 1997, Outstanding Seasonal Program in 1999 and Outstanding Community Program in 2012. In 2017, our former Executive Director, Lynn Handy, was awarded US Sailing's Virginia Long award for her efforts to improve sailing education at the national level. 

We are located in the heart of Baltimore at the Baltimore Museum of Industry, within easy walking distance from the Downtown, Federal Hill, South Baltimore, Riverside, and Locust Point neighborhoods. - DSC website

Founded in 1898, Chicago Booth is the second-oldest business school in the U.S. and is associated with 10 Nobel laureates in the Economic Sciences, more than any other business school in the world.[3][4]

The University of Chicago Graham School of Continuing Liberal and Professional Studies (previously the Continuing Education Division) is the school of continuing education at the University of Chicago. The Graham School's focus is on part-time and flexible programs of study. - Wikipedia

The Graham School offers Master of Liberal Arts degree programs, academic certificate programs, and a variety of credit and non-credit courses for graduate students at large, returning scholars, and adult learners. The Graham School manages the Summer Session, a series of academic programs for high school students, visiting college students, and international students. It conducts lecture series and other programs throughout the year.

The school's administrative offices can be found on the University of Chicago's main campus in the Hyde Park neighborhood.

The University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) is a public university in College Park, Maryland, United States, and the largest institution in the University System of Maryland. Established in 1947 as the College of Special and Continuation Studies of the University of Maryland, College Park, UMGC is dedicated to serving working adults, military service members, veteran and their families. UMGC offers online, hybrid, and face-to-face instruction at education centers across the Washington–Baltimore metropolitan area, throughout Maryland, and around the world.

UMGC is open to all applicants for undergraduate and graduate programs, and is among the top 10 recipients of the federal G.I. Bill benefits. The university offers 135 academic programs in online, hybrid and face-to-face classes, including bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees, as well as undergraduate and graduate certificates. UMGC is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. - Wikipedia

Gilman School is an all-boys independent, day, college preparatory school located in the Roland Park neighborhood of Baltimore, Maryland, United States. There are three school divisions: Lower School, grades pre-kindergarten through five; Middle School, grades six through eight; and Upper School, grades nine through twelve. Founded in 1897 as the Country School for Boys, it was the first country day school in the US. It is named for Daniel Coit Gilman, the first president of Johns Hopkins University and an early supporter of efforts by Anne Galbraith Carey to form an all-boys day school.

Gilman enrolls approximately 1,400 students, ranging from pre-kindergarten to 12th grade, under the instruction of 146 faculty members. It is a member of the Association of Independent Maryland Schools and the Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association. - Wikipedia

Calvert School, founded in 1897, is an independent, non-sectarian, co-educational lower and middle school located in Baltimore, Maryland. Calvert School is a member of the National Association of Independent Schools (NAIS) as well as the Association of Independent Maryland and DC Schools (AIMS).

History
Established in 1896 when four Baltimore families hired German school teacher Fraulein Martha Auguste Schurmann to conduct traditional kindergarten classes for their children, Calvert School continues to build upon the foundation laid by Fraulein Schurmann. The first children were taught above Croft and Conlin's drug store. In 1899, Calvert School hired its first Headmaster, Virgil M. Hillyer. - Wikipedia

St. Mary's Seminary and University is a Catholic seminary located within the Archdiocese of Baltimore in Baltimore, Maryland; it was the first seminary founded in the United States after the Revolution and has been run since its founding by the Society of the Priests of Saint Sulpice. - Wikipedia

publications.title: Activating the Workplace: The Impact of Active Workstations on Employee Effectiveness
publications.description: Today’s workforce understands that sitting all day is not healthy. As a result, employees are increasingly requesting more opportunities for movement throughout the workday. Workplace design has evolved to address sedentary behavior through active workstations, which allow individuals to experience the benefits of movement and posture change while engaging in productive work. Research on the health impacts of active workstations is well established, and most studies show an inverse relationship between the availability of active workstations and workers’ sedentary behavior. However, evidence of how these interventions impact employees beyond reducing sedentary behavior is still emerging. This paper contributes to this developing body of research by providing an overview of how active workstations affect an individual’s ability to effectively perform everyday job responsibilities. For the purposes of this paper, active workstations are defined as height-adjustable and treadmill desks. To explore the relationship between active workstations and employee effectiveness, a literature search was conducted. Articles were reviewed if they were published in a peer-reviewed journal within the past 10 years, analyzed more than just sedentary behavior, and were generalizable to the workplace. Findings suggest that height-adjustable desks have a neutral or positive impact on cognitive function and productivity/performance, and a positive impact on psychological outcomes, such as mood or energy levels. Research on the relationship between treadmill desks and employee effectiveness is still emerging, but preliminary evidence suggests that treadmill desks have a neutral or positive effect on cognitive function and psychological outcomes like boredom and satisfaction, and a mixed impact on productivity/performance. More robust, long-term studies are necessary to determine the impact that active workstations have on employee effectiveness over time.

headline: Customer Success Leader | Trusted Partner & Revenue Driver | Turning Clients Into Long-Term Partners | Solutions Engineering Mindset
about:
As a customer success leader, I thrive on building trust, driving adoption, and turning satisfied clients into long-term partners. I make it a priority to act as an extension of each client’s team—fully understanding their needs and challenges—so I can deliver real value at every stage, from onboarding through renewal and beyond.

I’m relentless about helping customers get the most out of what they’ve invested in. Whether it’s designing smarter onboarding, leading tailored training, or partnering with product teams to solve real client challenges, I’m here to make sure we deliver on what we promise — and then some.

Curiosity is my edge. I dive deep to understand how clients work, what they care about, and where we can help them grow. By combining that consultative mindset with a knack for translating product features into real business value, I help teams drive retention, expand accounts, and build relationships that stick.

Who am I beyond work? I bring the same energy and go-getter spirit to my life outside the office. I’m sharpening my culinary skills with the goal of becoming the next Stanley Tucci, often exploring farmers markets and getting creative with fresh, in-season ingredients. When I’m not cooking, you’ll find me training for a marathon or rehearsing for my next dance performance — my goal-oriented mindset keeps me moving and striving in every part of life.

My goal? To make every client feel like they’re part of something better than they expected. If you’re as passionate about customer success, solutions engineering, SaaS growth, and building lasting partnerships as I am — let’s connect.

Over the course of his 30-plus year career at Bain & Company, he worked with management teams to develop and execute growth strategies, evaluate acquisitions and divestitures, improve capabilities and implement organizational change. He has assisted clients across numerous industries, including retail, consumer products, telecommunications, automotive and media and entertainment.

Michael has also served on a number of Bain's governance committees, including its Board of Directors, Compensation and Promotion Committee, Global Operating Committee and Investment Committee.

Michael currently serves on the Board of Directors of Jacobs Solutions, Inc. as well as the Boards of Trustees of The Bridgespan Group and the Lincoln Park Zoo.

about:
With over 8 years of experience in the financial and business sectors, I am a seasoned economist known for my analytical rigor and creative solutions. My career began in the dynamic capital markets of Argentina, where my curiosity and drive for excellence led me to earn the CFA credential in just three years. At Max Capital as a Senior Corporate Sales & Trading, I navigated complex financial landscapes and changing regulations, advising a diverse portfolio of clients across industries such as healthcare, mining, agribusiness, oil & gas, and consumer retail. My approach combines deep financial analysis with innovative strategies for financing, hedging, cash management, and tax planning.

My diverse interests have also led me to explore entrepreneurship, co-creating a wine label and venturing into textile retail. Additionally, I've engaged in a digital art initiative with Kellogg MBA colleagues, enhancing how art is experienced. This project underscores my enthusiasm for tech-driven ventures.

Having completed an MBA at HEC Paris with an academic exchange at Northwestern Kellogg, I am excited to contribute as a strategic consultant at Bain & Company in São Paulo. I am deeply passionate about promoting sustainability in AgriTech and Foods & Beverages, leveraging innovation and strategic collaborations to create lasting value and impact.

----------
Con más de 8 años de experiencia en los sectores financiero y empresarial, soy un economista destacado por mi rigor analítico y creatividad en las soluciones. Comencé mi carrera en los dinámicos mercados de capitales de Argentina, logrando la certificación CFA en apenas tres años. Como Senior en Max Capital, manejé desafíos financieros complejos y regulaciones cambiantes, brindando asesoramiento a clientes corporativos de multiples sectores y tamaños. Implementé estrategias efectivas de financiamiento, cobertura, cashflow e impositivas.

También me aventuré en el emprendimiento, donde asesoré restaurantes, co-cree mi propia vino e incursioné en el retail textil. Actualmente, participo en un proyecto de arte digital con compañeros del MBA, orientado a tecnologizar la experiencia artística. Este proyecto resalta mi interés por las startups tecnológicas.

Tras completar un MBA en HEC París y mi paso por Northwestern Kellogg, pronto me incorporaré a Bain & Company en São Paulo como consultor estratégico. Estoy profundamente comprometido con la sostenibilidad en los sectores de AgriTech y Alimentos y Bebidas, promoviendo la innovación y colaboraciones estratégicas para generar un impacto duradero.

He has worked with clients on restructuring, international growth strategies, cross border expansion, organisational effectiveness, customer strategies, mergers & acquisitions, and change management. headline: Manager at Bain & Company
about:
I am a scientist and consultant interested in how businesses & science together can solve tough problems. 

As a Manager at Bain & Company, my work has been focused on growth strategy and propensity modeling to predict sales behavior. Past work at Bain was in the energy, natural resources, chemicals, and healthcare industries, where I have helped address challenges in corporate growth strategy, operational performance, and organization design. Additionally, I have worked on 10+ commercial due diligence projects as part of Bain’s Private Equity Group, specifically focused on companies in the healthcare, pharma, retail, fintech, cryptocurrency / web3, and recycling industries.

Prior to Bain, I was an A. O. Beckman postdoctoral fellow in biophysics & chemistry at the University of Chicago, and received my Ph.D. in chemistry from Caltech. My research worked to understand quantum mechanical effects in complex chemical systems, with specific expertise in laser spectroscopy, quantum chemistry, & machine learning.

slides.title: Post-Quarantine Recovery for Foodservice Distributors
slides.subtitle: Louis Bourassa on LinkedIn
slides.description: The foodservice industry has been one of the hardest-hit industries by the quarantine. In fact, in this white paper by Technomic it estimates a drop in 18% to 26% of consumer spending in 2020 for the sector. Technomic estimates a drop in 18% to 26% of consumer spending in 2020 for the foodservice sector. The paper also discusses how different market segments are expected to reopen and recover over time. The short answer is that it will be a very mixed bag with some segments recovering much faster (e.g., hospitals and refreshments services) than others (e.g., recreation and hotel). With the expected high variability in the location and volume of demand, foodservice distributors will struggle with maintaining transportation efficiency (maximizing pieces per trip) if they use a fixed routing methodology. The graphics below show an example of changes in demand for a foodservice distributor in Baltimore, MD. Aside from fewer deliveries, it is also expected the deliveries will drop in size. Routes that were efficient on March 8th are completely inadequate for the deliveries on May 8th. What To Do? Here are some ideas for foodservice distributors, or any other distribution business operating their own fleet, to alleviate the issue: Develop regional and localized strategies to determine the vulnerability of the business and the likely timeline for reopening. Work with your customers on payment flexibility, order minimums, etc. Operators that survive this pandemic will look to work with distributors that displayed partnership with them. Adopt dynamic routing as a means to adapt to the changing demands of your customers. If you have questions on how to take these steps, JBF Consulting can help you with the selection of the right technology, setting up your team with the necessary knowledge to succeed or doing the analytics (e.g., dynamic routing) for you. slides.title: TMS and ERP Implementations
slides.subtitle: Louis Bourassa on LinkedIn
slides.description: by Louis Bourassa ERP implementations are notoriously difficult to tackle. The list of failed projects is long and makes for entertaining, if lurid, reading: The Biggest ERP Failures of All Time, Eric Kimberling and ERP disaster zone: The mostly costly failures of the past decade, Lindsay Clark. While TMS implementations may not be at the same level of complexity (and certainly don’t garner as much attention) as ERPs, there are many similarities that can be drawn between the two. A study conducted by the Panorama Consulting Group, The 2020 ERP Report, found that of responding organizations that conducted an ERP implementation, 79% rated process change as being very difficult or difficult compared to 66% for organizational change and 34% for technical change. The most well-intentioned new technology won’t overcome people’s resistance to change. Based on my experience and those of my colleagues at JBF Consulting, the same holds true for TMS implementations. Software vendors will be quick to vaunt the ease of integration of their software. Especially with hosted systems, the technical aspects of integration are getting easier and quicker. However, the real difficulty lies in changing the well-entrenched processes and company culture that legacy systems have created. It is not something often considered by software vendors when they quote their implementation times. One workaround I have observed many times is to have the new system replicate the functionality of the old system. While this may minimize the need for process change, more often than not it also minimizes the impact of the new TMS. This is one reason why many TMS implementations do not achieve the expected benefits that justified the project in the first place. For example, during one project I’ve worked on, the client was adamant about having the Shipment Expected Delivery date provided via the ERP system because “this is how we’ve always done it.” In a way, this neutered the ability for the Customer Service function to take advantage of the new TMS and provide a richer response such as where the shipment currently was and if there had been any delays in transportation thus far (I’m simplifying the situation here for the sake of brevity). In conclusion, be weary of TMS software vendors and others promising quick implementation times. They may not be considering all the work that will have to be done in terms of process and organizational changes. Using an independent third-party services firm can help alleviate this issue. However, heed the advice of the vendors and consultants when considering the use of the new software’s functionalities. If you want to make full use of the TMS capabilities, you may have to make some difficult process changes. The benefit can far outweigh the effort in the long run. Just make sure the project schedule leaves enough time and resources to properly tackle this challenging aspect. Louis Bourassa is the Analytics & Optimization Practice Head at JBF Consulting. headline: Sr. Specialist - DEI Talent Acquisition
topSkills: Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) • Storytelling • Event Planning • Facilitation • Community Engagement
about:
I’m an equitable talent strategist, educator, artist, and advocate for systems-level justice, based in the Greater Boston area. My career began in Chicago’s theatre for young audiences scene, where I worked as a production stage manager, teaching artist, and arts administrator with a youth empowerment and anti-adultism focus. I’ve held roles at organizations like Chicago Children’s Theatre, Adventure Stage Chicago, Mudlark Theater, and Filament Theatre, where I served as a board member and chaired the Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Access committee.

I also have a background in sexual health and sexual violence prevention education, grounded in the reproductive justice framework defined by Black women activists in Chicago in the 90's. Through collaborations with the Illinois Caucus for Adolescent Health and Northwestern University, I have co-created participatory theatre experiences that merge education, performance, and activism in youth-centered spaces.

Since 2018, I’ve translated these values into the corporate world. I’m currently a Senior Specialist on Bain & Company’s DEI Talent Acquisition Center of Excellence team, where I lead bias-aware hiring initiatives, support inclusive recruiting strategies, and partner with community talent organizations. I also develop and facilitate DEI trainings and affinity group programming, including co-leading Pride at Bain in the Boston office and proudly serving as the firm’s inaugural Global Trans & Non-binary Lead.

My work is rooted in inclusive storytelling, systems thinking, and a commitment to building spaces where everyone can thrive. Outside of work, you can find me in the woods or at the beach, cooking for people I love, or working through the ever-growing stack of books on my bedside table.

publications.title: An exploratory study of sequence alignment for improved sensor based human activity recognition
publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of Construction Research Congress · Mar 1, 2018
publications.description: Sequence alignment (SA) is a well-established technique in bioinformatics for analyzing deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), ribonucleic acid (RNA), or protein sequences and identifying regions of similarity. The main goal of SA is to discover relationships between strings of data by deploying a series of heuristic or probabilistic methods to align a new string (e.g. DNA of a new species) with an existing string (DNA of a known species). SA has also been used sporadically in linguistics, social sciences, and finance. In this paper, the authors explore the prospect of coupling machine learning (ML) and SA to improve the output of human activity recognition (HAR) methods. In particular, several field experiments are conducted to collect heterogeneous human motion data via wearable sensors. Collected data is further mined using ML to identify sequences of activities performed in each experiment. Given the inaccuracy of sensor readings and the limitations of ML algorithms especially in handling datasets from complex human activities such as those performed by construction workers, it is expected that the resulting activity sequences not fully match actual activity sequences as observed in the field. To further clean up this inherent noise, SA is deployed to refine imperfections in the resulting activity sequences by manipulating the output of HAR and ultimately aligning noisy activity sequences with ground truth sequences. The outcome of this work is a systematic method to improve the reliability of HAR from sensor readings, which can benefit decision-making as related to task planning, resource management, productivity monitoring, and ergonomic assessment.

publications.title: BIM adoption by public facility agencies: impacts on occupant value
publications.publishedAt: Building Research and Information Journal · Mar 8, 2017
publications.description: Many governments have begun to demand that large public facility agencies adopt and implement building information modelling (BIM) in their business processes. Some have published BIM guides. Most of these are technical specifications that are useful at the project level, but they provide no support for the organization-level adoption effort. On the basis of a literature review, action research and case studies of five large UK government facility agencies, a BIM adoption impact map (BIM AIM) is proposed. It describes a set of possible relationships between the actions taken by public facility agencies, the intermediate outcomes of their actions and the eventual achievement of value for the occupants of the facilities they build. BIM AIM can be used by public facility agencies with a wide variety of construction project types to analyse and visualize the strengths, weaknesses and opportunities in their BIM adoption efforts, potentially enabling them to focus on social impacts and outcomes rather than on the technological or management actions that intermediate stakeholders promote.

publications.title: A review of building information modeling protocols, guides and standards for large construction clients
publications.description: Large construction clients (companies, public authorities and government departments) perceive the need to facilitate and accelerate adoption of Building Information Modeling (BIM) for their projects because they derive significant benefits from its use for design, construction and operation of their facilities. Preparation of appropriate BIM guidelines that can be mandated through contracts is one of the main steps they can take to promote adoption. With a view to aiding such organizations to compile comprehensive guideline documents, we present a qualitative content analysis of fifteen BIM guideline, standard and protocol documents published to date, identifying both common features and missing aspects. While the main topics covered are similar across all the standards and guides – interoperability, collaboration modes, BIM execution plan, simulation & analysis, BIM manager’s role and operation & maintenance requirements – their content, specificity, frequency and level of resolution are different. The category and topic analysis led to derivation of a set of essential requirements. Recommendations are provided to help organizations/governments compile their own documents and establish policies compatible with their specific context and needs.

projects.title: Ionoregulatory Responses of Atlantic Silversides (M. menidia) to Ocean Acidification Conditions
projects.description: Increasing levels of carbon released into the atmosphere by human activity has resulted in the earth’s oceans becoming more acidic and warmer. How fish respond to these ocean changes at a molecular level is not fully understood. However, it is known that producing more or fewer proteins is a way to respond to environmental stress, and the instructions for making these proteins are determined by a process called gene expression. This experiment investigated the impact of acidity and temperature of water on gene expression in Atlantic silverside (M. menidia) fish, a species that is responsive to environmental conditions. The genes examined in the experiment control the production of proteins that are important for maintaining chemical balance. Larval silverside samples were raised under experimental conditions representing three levels of acidity and of temperature. Results revealed which genes had a change in expression under these conditions, and which were unaffected. Additionally, different patterns of effect were observed in fish samples of different ages, suggesting processes that may emerge during the development of silverside fish that enable them to respond to changes in the surrounding ocean. Results confirm that changes in ocean acidity and temperature can affect marine organisms at a molecular level.

about:
As a seasoned strategist and marketing leader with over a decade of experience, I bring a unique blend of brand-building expertise, analytical rigor, and a passion for driving growth. My background spans global brands and leading management consulting, delivering impact across multiple industries.

At Nike, I primarily focused on brand marketing and strategy, with experience across nearly all business units. I spent most of my time on Nike Running and Nike Women's, developing impactful campaigns and driving brand growth. Additionally, I spent a portion of my time on the retail brand team, working on North American retail strategies for Nike Direct and wholesale partners. Throughout, I collaborated with cross-functional teams to bring Nike’s stories to life and deliver measurable results.

Currently, as a Consultant at Bain & Company, I have worked across industries, including private equity, healthcare, insurance, and financial services. My experience has deepened my analytical rigor and strengthened my ability to develop strategic insights and drive organizational change.

My MBA from Chicago Booth further strengthened my approach to tackling complex challenges and fostering collaborative innovation. I thrive on solving big problems, bringing people together, and delivering impact through strategic thinking and creative execution.

about:
As a versatile professional with +7 years of experience across management consulting, journalism, and policymaking, I bring a unique perspective and diverse skill set, particularly in strategic thinking, business strategy, project management, and communications.

Currently, I work as a consultant at Bain & Co. where I have worked with clients from a variety of industries (including financial services, enterprise tech, healthcare, retail and social impact) to develop innovative solutions that drive growth, improve operational efficiency, and add long-term value. I have strong expertise in data analytics, project management, change management, and organizational design.

Previously, I worked at the United Nations as a consultant, developing and implementing public policy at the local, national, and international levels, including managing stakeholder engagement and writing policy briefs. Before the UN, I was an investigative journalist, where I had to uncover the truth and present complex information in an accessible way. I have exceptional research, analytical, and communication skills, and an ability to craft compelling narratives that resonate with diverse audiences.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to driving positive change and delivering high-impact solutions that meet the needs of organizations and communities alike. If you catch me outside of work, I am a trained Barre instructor and an avid traveler. I also like meeting people over an oat milk latte -- feel free to reach out at allishaazlan@gmail.com

headline: Bain & Company | Chicago Booth MBA | Veteran
about:
My journey to leadership has been unconventional.

I am a combination of experience in direct sales, customer service, HR management, long-term strategy, and a lot more. Fortunately, I was able to gain all of that from just two massive organizations: The Home Depot Contact Center and the U.S Army.

I grew up wishing that I received more development from people around me. I didn’t start receiving real development from a personal or leadership/success perspective until I was almost a man. Before then, the majority was self-development. Starting with the first opportunity I had to lead a team, I’ve loved helping people better themselves personally and professionally.

I have over 7 years of experience in various forms of operations management. Starting with People Leading in contact operations wherein my responsibilities included honing the skills of my people to not just meet and exceed business targets in sales and service, but to also develop personal/professional skills that would prepare them to take the next step in their individual careers.

I then shifted to People Leading in the Military. The wide scope of responsibility demanded me to hone my skills in human resource management and develop skills in cross-functional planning, long-term strategy, decision-making, and cost management. I accomplished this by taking lead on planning efforts across separate professions and teams with limited resources, executing the plan to completion, and turning abstract ideas into concrete value for key stakeholders.  I have overseen operations at organizations ranging in size from 500 to 4000 personnel, managed teams of 40-150 people, and worked with 3-7 direct reports.

I look forward to learning more about managing operations and developing leaders in all aspects of business. Don’t hesitate to connect and share something with me!

headline: Accomplished Board Leader, Transformational Executive, Advisor
about:
Angel serves as Executive Chairman of LevaData Inc. and as an Independent Director of Peloton Interactive (NASDAQ: PTON, Chair - Audit Committee), SleepNumber (NASDAQ: SNBR, Chair - NomGov Committee), and Kinaxis (TSX: KXS, Lead Director). 

A visionary leader with over 35 years of experience driving innovation, operational excellence, and enterprise transformation, Angel thrives at the intersection of software, Industry 4.0 technologies, and real-world industrial and consumer applications. His leadership spans some of the world’s most recognized technology firms and diverse industries, including technology, financial services, and industrial sectors. 

In his most recent operating role, Angel was EVP and COO of HERE Technologies, leading a $1 billion P&L, global operations, product management, and its corporate transformation program. Prior to that, he spent a decade in senior leadership roles at Cisco Systems, where he spearheaded the company’s enterprise transformation program and led its global Supply Chain operations. Earlier in his career, Angel built a solid foundation during 12 years with GE, graduating from its prestigious Manufacturing Management Program, and held senior executive roles at AlliedSignal (now Honeywell), Citigroup, Gateway, and Palm.

Professional Expertise and Achievements:

-Turnaround Leadership & P&L Accountability: Proven track record in driving top-line growth, operational optimization, and business transformation across organizations with revenues ranging from $30M to $50B.
-Innovation & Execution Excellence: Deep expertise in business model innovation, strategic partnerships, value chain optimization, and enhancing customer and stakeholder engagement.
-Building High-Performing Teams: Known for creating winning cultures through talent development and fostering unity toward ambitious goals.
-Honored Executive: Named one of the “Top 20 Most Influential Hispanics in Corporate America.”

Leadership in Civic and Educational Initiatives:

Angel is dedicated to advancing education and civic engagement. He is a member of the Board of Trustees at Lafayette College, where he served six years as Secretary and Executive Officer. His past board affiliations include the Association of Governing Boards of Universities and Colleges (AGB) and the P33 Chicago initiative, aimed at driving economic growth and technology innovation.

slides.title: CEO’s Take Heed: You are now supply chain risk managers
slides.subtitle: Angel L. Mendez on LinkedIn
slides.description: COVID-19 has catapulted CEO's to the role of supply chain risk manager. But are they prepared to fund readiness? On April 12th, the legendary former CEO of Cisco Systems, and my former boss, John Chambers, contributed an excellent and timely article to the digital version of Fortune. Referring to the criticality of supply chain risk management practices in the Covid-19 crisis, he said the following: “The coronavirus pandemic has caused delays and other frustrations in businesses’ global supply chains, highlighting how vulnerable many are to unexpected disruption. Companies caught flat-footed should learn their lesson from this crisis and begin making fundamental changes now to prepare their supply chains for future shocks.” John often speaks on CEO best practices and he is always spot on. Relying on his concept of the “Power of the And,” he reminds us not only to play defense but also go on offense and leverage the crisis to leap ahead of competitors. (Author's pro tip: for more on then idea of the “Power of the And” I recommend the book "Doing Both" by my friend and former colleague Inder Sidhu). The playbooks for supply chain risk planning and mitigation that John mentions in his article were based on Cisco’s experience managing through a number of incredibly difficult supply chain disruptions. To be successful in mitigating these events, one has to install and operate a formal, data-centric, technology-enabled process that can be immediately deployed. The process must be inextricably linked to a broader Enterprise Risk Management framework, which must be regularly rehearsed and stress tested. Having led global operations for many years at companies like GE, Allied Signal and Palm, I thought I was well grounded in the art of supply chain resiliency. I had joined Cisco not long after managing through the well-documented SARS disruption in 2003. As head of Cisco’s supply chain from 2005 to 2011, my team and I managed a series of unprecedented events that tested every bit of our readiness and helped us build best in class capabilities. Supply chain risk historians will note that it was during this period that supply chain leaders managed through the following series of events: -Chengdu Earthquake (May 2008): -Great Recession (late 2008 to mid-2010) -Iceland Volcano Eruptions (April - May 2010) -H1N1 (April 2009-August 2010) -Fukushima Earthquake and Nuclear/Energy Crisis (April 2011) I am proud to say that despite the severity of these events, Cisco’s supply chain team, led by exceptional operators like Kevin Harrington, John O'Connor, Karl Braitberg, Mark Brillhart, Jack Allen, Erich Shaffer, James Steele, Anne Robinson, Mike McGlynn, Dan Gilbert, Kathy Chin Makranyi, Jeff Gallinat and many others, not only mitigated potential revenue and customer satisfaction risks, but also installed enduring capabilities that no doubt have been improved by current leadership. I was proud to lead and serve with such a talented group of leaders and supply chain practitioners. The processes and capabilities that resulted from managing these events have been well documented and shared in the public domain. Organizations like the Institute of Supply Management and publications like the SCM Review have covered these processes thoroughly, and Cisco has been exceptional at contributing its learnings. These best practices have also been incorporated into the business curriculum of several of America’s best universities, notably MIT and The Ross Business School at The University of Michigan. It is therefore fitting to re-share some of these references now given the depth of impact from Covid-19 (see links below). It is also important to note that two successful start-ups emerged from these learnings. Levadata and Resilinc, led by former Cisco supply chain leaders Rajesh Kalidindi and Bindiya Vakil respectively, offer their customers AI-centric capabilities that are integral to resilient supply chain management processes. https://www.instituteforsupplymanagement.org/files/richterawards/ciscosubmissionsupportdoc2012.pdf http://webuser.bus.umich.edu/anupindi/cases/GL1428881I_Cisco.pdf https://usresilienceproject.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/pdf-USRP_Cisco_Japan_CS_022912.pdf https://ctl.mit.edu/pub/newsletter/supply-chain-frontiers-49-case-study-proactive-risk-management While it is instructive to look backwards at these events and best practices, CEO’s and their supply chain leaders must think about what will be different in the post Covid-19 world. My personal view is that the Covid-19 crisis will force the acceleration of a number of supply chain trends that were already underway due to other risks and events. For example, much has been said in the last few days about “reshoring” from China. Some have even claimed that “the end of globalization” is upon us. The truth is that many companies have been geographically rebalancing their supply chains for some time, driven principally by market trends, talent availability, tax policy changes, cyber risks in China and other parts of Asia, and, more recently, trade and tariff effects. Covid-19 will accelerate this trend, but there will be other fundamental shifts as well. Supply Chain Trends Accelerated by the Covid-19 crisis: Supply chain architectures will grow in complexity. In addition to geographic rebalancing (“relocalization”) and redundancy priorities causing shifts in supply chain nodes (plants, distribution centers, etc.), today’s common supply chain architectures (build to stock, configure to order, build to order) will further “hybridize” across many industries. This will allow companies to manage for risk while maintaining fulfillment requirements and ensuring customer satisfaction. We have seen this phenomenon for a number of years, with perhaps the most notable example being the customer driven “omni channel” capabilities in the retail space. You’ll see hybrids emerge everywhere and this will require improved integrated planning and execution systems, increased agility and supply chain visibility enhancements. This architectural complexity will further complicate multi-vendor/multi-tier orchestration as companies attempt to synchronize demand and supply across a more complex network. The good news is that technology solutions exist to help manage this complexity. In full disclosure, I am a member of the board of directors of Kinaxis, the leading supply chain software provider in this space. Demand for these mission critical applications will intensify as supply chain operators cope with demand signal volatility and supply chain disruptions. Every company will want to be equipped with real time, end to end visibility technology. Even if supply chain planning is fully optimized, unless you know where everything is, all the time, the chain is still sub-optimal and unable to respond to risk events at full speed. Without end-to end visibility, chains will struggle to “self-heal” in real time, adding delay in recovery especially when factories and professional workforces are disrupted by crisis and when demand signal accuracy is anyone’s best guess. Thanks to companies like FourKites, Project44 and others, much has improved in some aspects of real time supply chain visibility. That said, there are still huge blind spots. Invisible inbound and outbound shipments, hampered by un-integrated location data, still exist in most supply chain flows. My own company, Here Technologies, is addressing this gap with products like Here Tracking, but much more remains to be done as firms integrate status signals into their planning and execution systems. Without this real time integration, supply chains will take much longer to cope with massive crisis-driven demands. There is simply too much reliance on manual intervention. Risk management capital and operating expenses will be challenged. Corporate financial priorities do not incent supply chain organizations to invest in risk management and readiness. Buffer stocks, targeted at risk events, are expensed in the same manner as stocks targeted for revenue. Any extra investment in safety stocks are charged to OPEX as incurred and are subject to the same price variance risks. It is hard for supply chain leaders to pay for “just in case” stock, yet for many industries this will be critical, especially when it comes to the health care industry. The same goes for extra capital equipment that would be bought and stored in the event of factory disruptions. When supply chain professionals do "Time-To-Recovery” analysis, recovery speed is almost always throttled by the lead-time needed to acquire the capital equipment required to transfer capacity away from risk spots. The contingent action is to buy and store bottleneck capital, “just in case.” As this capital gets the same accounting treatment as every other kind, corporate P&L’s pay a price for investing in risk management. There is no forgiveness on the P&L for investing in risk recovery capability. Risk preparedness costs money, and ROI calculations aren’t exactly straightforward. I believe companies will feel other financial pressures, especially on continuity insurance costs. Insurers will likely double down on their analysis of supply chain risk management programs and will likely reset premiums according to their assessment of risk management capabilities. Audit Oversight: Much in the same way as cyber security readiness has risen to high priority for corporate audit partners, supply chain risk management will be much more scrutinized. The likes of KPMG, EY and others will likely equip themselves with enhanced audit capabilities that can more adequately penetrate corporate processes to assess risk management programs. Wall Street Interest: Analysts will inspect companies more closely for supply chain redundancy and readiness. Wall street watchdogs, like ISS, will care more about the details of supply chain risk. Deeper questions are likely to be asked in earnings calls and investor events. So how will CEO’s be tested? With 35 years of technology and industrial leadership experience, I can confidently say that most CEO's care deeply about supply chain risk management. Sadly, very few actually show sufficient interest in the details except at a time of crisis. Even fewer understand the relationship between their P&L and supply chain risk, much less the level of investment required to “buy down” risk and stand up “on call” readiness capabilities and technologies. Furthermore, many CEO’s are still not well informed when it comes to their supply chain dynamics. A recent survey of Chief Supply Chain Officers conducted by EgonZehnder across multiple industries and 23 countries, revealed that despite their criticality to their business, only 53% of supply chain officers report directly to the CEO. While these results represent significant progress in the last decade on this dimension, many supply chain organizations are still not represented at the top of senior leadership's agenda. So yes, CEO’s are now supply chain risk managers. In addition to setting strategy and managing the talent agenda, the CEO’s main role is to allocate resources. Now is the time for CEO’s to understand the dynamics of supply chain risk and support their CSCO with the needed capability and technology capital despite the uncertain ROI. They will be thankful the next time a massive risk hits. So will their investors. One last thing. We can’t help but be in awe of our health care workers as we live through the horrific effects of the Covid-19 pandemic. Across the world, often working without the needed supplies and equipment, first responders, nurses, doctors, lab technicians and front-line workers, are working day and night to treat the infected and save lives. Not a day goes by when we don’t see and hear stories of selfless heroism, with many putting their lives at risk to save others. They deserve our humble admiration and thanks whether or not we or our families have been directly affected by this cruel disease. That said, I feel it’s also important to note the heroic work that supply chain and logistics management teams around the world are doing right now. Most are working around the clock, managing risk war rooms, keeping their employees safe, dealing with factory absenteeism, and even shifting plants to make ventilators or sanitizer. They are handling massive capacity and logistics constraints, all in the service of keeping shelves stocked with the food, essential supplies, and medicines the rest of us count on. I know many of these leaders and how committed they are to their craft. People like Dave Clark at Amazon and Greg Smith at Walmart lead exceptional global teams that are working around the clock and under enormous stress. They are supported by amazing leaders like John Church, Marc Engel, Sandra MacQuillan, Beth Ford, Kathy Wengel, Mike Corbo, Yanniss Koufalus and many, many others. These are some of the supply chain warriors on the front line of this crisis. They, and their teams around the world, are heroes too.

publications.title: Inbound Marketing and SEO: Insights from the Moz Blog
publications.description:
As the SEO industry undergoes a shift and Google continues to change its algorithm, successful SEO practitioners need to increase their knowledge of a wide range of inbound marketing channels. The Moz Blog is the go-to place for the latest thought leadership on the shifts in inbound marketing and SEO. This book cherry-picks and updates the most popular articles for the key inbound marketing disciplines, mixing them with some brand-new essays. Rand Fishkin and Thomas Høgenhaven have produced a masterfully edited anthology packed with information to provide the best possible insight into these marketing channels. The popular Moz blog is a top resource for cutting-edge information on SEO techniques:

Co-compiled and co-edited by Moz CEO and co-founder Rand Fishkin, this book is an anthology of articles selected to provide the best possible overview of current SEO and inbound marketing techniques and trends
Covers channels of online marketing, content marketing, social media, outreach, conversion rate optimization, and analytics, as well as search engine optimization
Focuses on leveraging existing platforms like social media sites and community for inbound marketing success

Inbound Marketing and SEO is a must-have for marketers in today's online world.

Currently there are several segments of SEO strategy seen as optional that are actually absolutely imperative to the success of an SEO campaign, as well as to the synergy of other initiatives within the marketing mix. In other words, SEO must adopt and adapt in order to be taken seriously and command the type of influence required to drive change. As it stands, SEO looks to disrupt the symphony (or cacophony) that is a brand’s marketing mix. Let’s discuss a new process that allows SEO to improve the effectiveness of all digital marketing channels – not just inbound.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Leader | People | Talent | Learning | Culture | Coach | Business Partner | FLPI
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: March 25, 2024, Becky was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description:
I worked with Frank as my executive coach in 2023, at a crucial time in my role and career. Frank's support and challenge through this period were invaluable in helping me better understand myself; how I can be at my best and what may get in my way. 

Importantly, I always walked away with practical next steps to approach a situation or relationship differently as a result of the coaching. 

I valued and admired Frank's ability to deeply listen, and to create just the kind of space that I needed during each session. He also always offered up highly useful and relevant tools and resources to support what we explored in the coaching sessions, helping me to further embed what I'd taken on board. 

I highly recommend Frank as an executive coach for all these reasons.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Marketing Director - Unilever Food Solutions
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: November 1, 2023, Nihan was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description:
Frank has been my executive coach for six months as part of the Unilever Ezra Coaching Program. I've appreciated his friendly and collaborative style, which has helped me discover valuable insights about myself and improve in specific areas we've targeted.

Frank's direct questions have expanded my thinking with different perspectives. He's recommended useful books, videos, and articles that have stimulated my thinking and encouraged new viewpoints.

His approach has made it easier to confront real insights and develop fresh ideas. He emphasizes applying what we learn on the job, rather than just focusing on theory, which helps turn knowledge into habits.

Based on my positive experience, I'd recommend working with him.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: General Manager
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: September 19, 2023, Daniel was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: Frank is the type of coach a leader wants to have at his site when it really counts. Frank is not only frank... he also seems to have some kind of supernatural powers to sense and feel what really matters in difficult situations, and what deserves to take a closer look at. With Frank, I not only felt always save and understood, I also walk out of the coaching sessions with a feeling of calm and reassurance, able to tackle any so difficult situation in my professional life. The richness of methods, his wealth experience, and his concrete and practical tips makes his client's - me! - strive. He has an impressive ability to look at things from different angles, always focussing on making the most out of what is, helping his client to achieve what actually could be, helping them to become the best version of themselves - and more. Frank is a tremendous mentor and coach, and the north star of my growth and professional success over the past year.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Director, Legal & Compliance International
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: June 19, 2023, Ritu was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: Frank is an excellent executive coach, whose approach is understanding and compassionate, whilst simultaneously challenging thought processes and perceptions, leading to impactful change. I looked forward to our sessions and came away from each one having gained a new perspective or a new tool to help me to achieve the goals I had set for myself. The learnings I took away from our sessions have led to tangible successes and I’m so grateful for the opportunity to work with Frank. It was an honor and privilege, and I hope to work together again in the future.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: PhD, Global Head of Clinical Pharmacology, Statistics and DMPK at Ribocure
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: May 1, 2023, Lotta was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: I feel genuinely privileged to have had the opportunity to interact with Frank in his role as executive leadership coach. With his great presence, genuine and warm curiosity, and a deep expertise and experience in coaching and leadership, Franks coaching style really drives impactful insight, which I experienced first-hand. I was truly impressed by how efficiently and accurately Frank also identified and shared useful, easy-to-use-and-digest tools and knowledge based resources between sessions. I highly recommend Frank if you are looking for an executive coach to maximize your leadership potential.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: EHS Executive Leader at GE Vernova
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: November 10, 2022, Beyza was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: I worked with Frank as my executive coach. Frank helped me to further improve my self awareness and drive meaningful outcomes demonstrating the right leadership behaviors. He always stayed true to our purpose (objectives we set in the beginning) and ensured we meet those priorities. He built the trust in this coaching experience, where he made me feel very comfortable to share and have an open conversation on issues, which helped me bringing clarity and more effective problem solving. Many thanks to you Frank for supporting my journey at an important time, highly appreciated.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Chief Information Security Officer at Allianz Benelux
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: March 31, 2022, Marc was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: Frank coached me into some breakthrough insights about my personality that really helped me improve my overall effectiveness in a pleasant way. This was quite an odd experience: gaining really useful new insights about myself at age 57 (I thought I new it all).  Frank has been pragmatic and flexible in offering various methods and techniques to find the one that worked best for me. In our coaching engagement he was both patient and persistent, a great combination for a pleasant coaching journey with a high probability of real improvement. The improvement sticks, as I write this review 2 months after our engagement. Really happy I met Frank, he is the best executive coach/trainer I know.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Head of Perm Placement
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: December 8, 2021, Lisa was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: Frank is a great coach.  I worked with Frank for a month during which time we set measurable goals.  Frank gave me lots of tools and insight to help me on my development journey and checked in with me regularly.   Frank has a great sense of humour and is a pleasure to work with.  I highly recommend Frank to anybody looking for a coach to support their development.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Protective Security Mgmt & Outsourcing Officer bij Allianz Benelux
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: January 20, 2021, Adriaan was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: Frank is a great coach. He supported me very well in identifying my personal motives and boundaries. His clear approach and sharp observations have helped me to achieve my self proclaimed goals (he was very keen on me taking the lead in this). More important he gave me the tools to continue on the chosen path by myself. I am thankful he set the scene to open up.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Senior Legal Counsel at Greenpeace International | my posts are my own
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: January 17, 2021, Roos was Frank’s client
receivedRecommendations.description: Frank is a great coach. He stands out with his very personal and positive approach, his gentle (but open and honest) coaching style and his ability to make anyone feel safe and comfortable sharing their stories and thoughts. As a result, my coaching sessions with him were enriching, leading to valuable and deep personal insights that are of great value to me on a daily basis. He played an essential role in uncovering thought patterns and assumptions that I was unaware of (despite knowing myself, I think, quite well) but that were key to certain behavioral patterns that I really wanted to change. The coaching sessions yielded quick and effective results and changes that were easy to implement on a day-to-day basis, all in a very positive atmosphere.
